WordWake shows a message you write on your screen at the time you choose, with the sound you pick — even while you sleep, while the app is closed, or with no internet.\n\nTo do that reliably, Android needs a few permissions. Each one is explained below; you can change them at any time from Settings.
WordWake can show the alarm notification and your message.

Without notifications your alarm cannot show the message, open the alarm screen, or show Stop/Snooze buttons. The sound may still play, but you would not see why. If you denied it before, use “Open settings”.
Alerts start at the exact minute you choose, also in battery-saving idle mode.
Without this, Android decides when to deliver alerts and may delay them by several minutes or more — especially while the phone is idle overnight.
When the phone is locked or idle, the alarm can turn the screen on and show your message full screen.
Without this, the alarm appears only as a notification. You can tap it to open your message, but the screen may not turn on by itself.
Background use is restricted for WordWake. Alarms will likely not ring. Open the app’s settings → Battery and choose “Unrestricted” or “Optimised”.
Your phone’s alarm volume is loud enough. WordWake never changes it for you.
Your phone’s alarm volume is low, so you might not hear the alarm. WordWake does not change system volume itself.

Most phones deliver WordWake’s alarms normally. Some manufacturers (for example TECNO, Infinix, itel, Xiaomi, Huawei, Oppo, Vivo, OnePlus, Samsung) aggressively stop apps in the background. If alerts are late or missing, set WordWake to “Unrestricted” / “Don’t optimise”, and allow “Autostart” where your phone offers it.

This phone’s own battery manager can freeze WordWake and hold back its alarms, even exact ones (we observed this on a TECNO phone: the alarm never rang). Tap below and choose “Allow” so WordWake can run in the background. This only matters while an alarm is due; WordWake does no background work otherwise.

Your phone also has its own “Auto-start” or “App launch” switch that Android cannot report to apps. On TECNO, Infinix and itel: Phone Master → App management → Auto-start → allow WordWake, then Settings → Apps → WordWake → Battery → No restrictions. Afterwards, use “Test alert now” and a real 2-minute test message with the phone locked.
Battery Saver is on right now. Exact alarms still ring, but some phones also restrict background work in this mode.

• If the phone is switched off, no alert can appear until it is turned on again. A one-time alert missed this way is reported as “Missed” when the phone starts again.
• After a restart, alerts are restored once you unlock the phone for the first time.
• If you “Force stop” WordWake in Android settings, Android blocks all its alarms until you open the app again.
• The alarm screen appears on top of your lock screen but never unlocks your phone.
• Do Not Disturb normally lets alarms through, but this depends on your DND settings.
• Phone manufacturers can add their own restrictions that override app settings.

Your messages never leave this phone

WordWake uses Android’s alarm clock system, which is designed to ring on time even in deep sleep. Some phones add extra restrictions:

• Samsung: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → make sure WordWake is not in “Sleeping” or “Deep sleeping apps”.
• Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO: App info → Autostart ON; Battery saver → No restrictions.
• Huawei / Honor: Battery → App launch → WordWake → Manage manually, allow all.
• Oppo / Realme / OnePlus: App info → Battery → Allow background activity.
• TECNO / Infinix / itel: Phone Master → App management → Auto-start → allow WordWake; Settings → Battery → App battery management → WordWake → No restrictions. • Vivo: Battery → Background power consumption → allow WordWake.

Also:
• Don’t swipe-kill or “Force stop” the app with a cleaner app.
• Keep the alarm volume up; WordWake never changes it for you.
• Use “Test alert now” from a message’s menu to check sound and display on your phone.

• Your messages, schedules and settings are stored only on this phone.
• WordWake has no internet permission: it cannot upload anything, and it works fully offline.
• No accounts, analytics, ads or trackers.
• Audio files you pick are read in place through Android’s file picker; they are not copied or uploaded.
• The alarm screen and notification show your message on the lock screen while an alert is active, so anyone near the phone can read it then.
• Uninstalling WordWake deletes all of its data.
